diagnosis: Household purchase budget used fresh income only and excluded existing cash as a source for ongoing necessities
No-income households could retain large cash balances while their purchase plan became zero
Finite government buffer and one-way energy external account drain domestic circulation
Nominal employer relation is not proof of actual wage payment
Conservation of cash holds; long-run behavioral plausibility was not established
follow_up: Explicit household essential-consumption plan bounded by available cash; source-of-funds and fiscal accounting views. External exports and debt finance remain outside scope.
